items.title: Leonardo da Vinci, Manuscript B folio 83 verso: the 'aerial screw' (1883 facsimile)
items.creator: Leonardo da Vinci (drawing); facsimile ed. Charles Ravaisson-Mollien, Paris: A. Quantin, 1883
items.date: Drawing: Manuscript B, generally dated c. 1487-1490 (dating from standard literature, not from the source record); facsimile printed 1883
items.use_for: renaissance_sketch (hero: Leonardo flying machine with mirror writing; ideal for the drawing-to-blueprint trace)
items.depicts: Full printed page from the 1883 facsimile. Top: printed header '- FOLIO 83 (verso). -'. Centre: the sepia facsimile plate of the manuscript page: Leonardo's famous helical 'aerial screw' (a spiral sail on a mast over a round platform with diagonal hatching beneath it), drawn in brown ink, with a block of mirror-written notes to its left and below it, a smaller sketch of a horizontal flying device at the top with a mirror-written line above it, and a small '8' numeral. Below the plate: printed Italian transcription in ordinary type (to be cropped away) and printed page number 82. Very sharp at 100%: individual pen strokes and the mirror writing are crisp; slight paper mottling and a small light patch at top-right corner of the page. No people.
items.evidence: IA item lesmanuscritsdel02lo, page index n340 (title page OCR: 'Les Manuscrits B & D de la Bibliotheque de l'Institut publies en fac-similes (procede Arosa) avec transcription litterale, traduction francaise ... par M. Charles Ravaisson-Mollien, Paris, A. Quantin ... MDCCCLXXXIII'). The page header reads 'FOLIO 83 (verso)' and the printed transcription under the plate includes 'truovo secquesto strumento ... facto avite sara bene facto ... di tela lina stopata ... picciolo modello di charta ... ravolgiere la uite', i.e. Leonardo's note on the screw ('vite') instrument, confirming this is the aerial-screw folio. Downloaded at full scan size via archive.org/download/lesmanuscritsdel02lo/page/n340.jpg (scan 400 ppi).

Quantin, 1883 (title page 'MDCCCLXXXIII'; IA lists the series date 1881). items.depicts: Printed header '- FOLIO 74 (recto). -'. items.title: Leonardo da Vinci, Manuscript B folio 88 verso: bat-wing flying apparatus with a figure working a lever (1883 facsimile)

items.use_for: renaissance_sketch (alternate; the most 'flying machine' looking page, upper third is the hero area)
items.depicts: Printed header '- FOLIO 88 (verso). -'. Upper third of the plate: a large ribbed bat-like wing on a long beam/lever with a small seated human figure at its left end pushing on it, a pulley/scale apparatus above, a sweeping arc showing the wing's path, and a small standing figure near the centre. Below: about 20 lines of dense mirror-written text in brown ink, two ink blots at lower right, and at top right two lines of later handwriting in normal (not mirror) direction. Printed transcription below the plate (crop away). The tiny figures are sketched, not identifiable people.

(a test of wings of paper reinforced with netting, about 20 braccia wide). I describe the drawing visually and do not claim more about its purpose.

items.title: Leonardo da Vinci, Design for a Stage Setting (verso of 'Allegory on the Fidelity of the Lizard'), 1496 - The Met 17.142.2
items.creator: Leonardo da Vinci
items.use_for: renaissance_sketch (an ORIGINAL Leonardo sheet photographed by its holder; slow macro pans over genuine mirror writing and measurements)
items.depicts: Colour photograph of the actual sheet (landscape, cream paper, brown ink, thin white border and a small paper tab at the left edge). Upper left: about 12 lines of Leonardo's mirror writing with columns of numbers and fractions (measurements). Centre/left: a perspective sketch of a barrel-vaulted niche with a seated figure on a throne and side niches; right: a stage set with a coffered/curved upper structure, a framed opening with a small arch, and diagonal construction lines. Lower half of the sheet is blank paper with light staining. At 100% the pen lines and handwriting are crisp. Second file in the folder: DT232678.jpg = the recto (2523x3722), a roundel with a sleeping figure and a lizard under a tree, mirror writing across the top.

items.creator: Fra Luca Pacioli (author/artist per The Met); printed by Paganino Paganini; The Met lists 'after Leonardo da Vinci' as designer of the book's woodcuts
items.use_for: renaissance_to_blueprint (each capital is built from compass circles and a ruled square: ideal for the 'drawing becomes blueprint' beat; together they spell M-A-R-S-O-P-S for the title reveal)

Files: letter_M_DP156952.jpg (3358x3596), letter_A_DP156941.jpg (3027x4000), letter_R_DP156958.jpg (2645x3554), letter_S_DP156959.jpg (2555x3591), letter_O_DP156955.jpg (2405x3443), letter_P_DP156956.jpg (2446x3351); S is reused for the final S. items.title: Global Color Views of Mars (PIA00407), Viking Orbiter mosaic
items.creator: NASA/JPL/USGS
items.depicts: Full, evenly lit globe of Mars in true-ish colour on pure black, 6787x6787 TIFF. The disk nearly touches all four edges of the square frame. White north polar cap at top centre; dark Acidalia region upper right; the Valles Marineris canyon system crossing the lower half left to right; Tharsis volcanoes as round shields along the left limb; dark regions at lower right. Sharp detail (craters, channels) at full size. Rendered globe from a reprojected mosaic, not a single photo.

items.title: Incredible Solar Flare, Prominence Eruption and CME Event (304 angstroms), June 7, 2011 - SDO/AIA
items.creator: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio (animator Tom Bridgman, producer Scott Wiessinger, scientist William D. Pesnell); SDO/AIA data
items.use_for: radiation (hero: the Sun throwing off a flare and coronal mass ejection)
items.depicts: Real SDO/AIA 304 A ultraviolet time-lapse of the whole Sun, rendered red-orange on black, 4096x4096 HEVC, 30 fps, 11.97 s, no audio, no burned-in text. The textured disk fills ~85% of the frame with bright active regions top-centre and lower right. At ~0.7-1.0 s an M2 flare flashes at the lower-right limb and a huge spray of dark, cooler plasma blasts out over the limb (1.0-3.5 s), then rains back onto the surface (3.5-6 s); 6-12 s is a calmer disk with residual loops. One frame = one minute of real time.
items.evidence: SVS page 3838 (saved, plus API record svs_3838_record.json): 'On June 7, 2011, an M-2 flare occurred on the Sun which released a very large coronal mass ejection (CME). Much of the ejected material is much cooler (less than about 80,000K) and therefore appears dark against the brighter solar disk. Material which does not reach solar escape velocity can be seen falling back...'; dataset '304 Filter, 2011/06/07T06:00:00 - 2011/06/07T12:00:00'; 'Please give credit for this item to: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio'. File MonsterFilament_304A_4096p30_h265.mp4 (415,949,053 bytes). Frames checked at 0.0-6.0 s in 0.5 s steps plus 9 and 11.5 s; peak brightness in the eruption region at 1.0 s (measured).

NASA guidelines apply: no implied NASA endorsement.
items.credit_line: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio; data: NASA SDO/AIA
items.usable_ranges: Best 4 s: 0.6-4.6 s (flare flash at ~1.0 s, plasma spray 1.0-3.5 s, start of fall-back). Extended: 0.0-6.0 s. Calm disk: 6.0-12.0 s. No damaged frames seen. HEVC decode is heavy at 4K: transcode to an intermediate first. Eruption region approx rel x0.70-1.00, y0.42-0.72 (lower-right limb); a 9:16 crop of about 2304x4096 positioned right of centre keeps both the limb and the spray.

items.title: An X1.9 flare from AR 14114 - June 19, 2025 (SDO/AIA 171 angstroms)
items.creator: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio (data visualizer Tom Bridgman, producer Scott Wiessinger); SDO/AIA data
items.use_for: radiation (alternate, calmer and golden: coronal loops and plumes; matches a warm sepia palette better than the red 304 clip)
items.depicts: Real SDO/AIA 171 A time-lapse of the full Sun in gold on black, 2048x2048 H.264, 30 fps, 60 s, no audio, no burned-in text in this unstamped 'Flares_' version. Fine coronal loops arch off both limbs and long plumes stream from the right limb; a dark filament channel crosses the disk diagonally. The X1.9 flare is a brightening of compact loops in AR 14114 near the upper-right limb; it is modest at full-disk scale (crop in to sell it).

notes: 11 items, all commercial-use safe with no claims: 3 Leonardo Manuscript B pages (public-domain 1883 facsimile; original in Paris, not Italy), 1 original Leonardo sheet + 1 Pacioli 1509 book (The Met, CC0), and 6 NASA public-domain items (Viking Mars, 2 SDO videos, xEMU photo, EMU line drawing, Mars habitat concept). Rules for the edit: (1) mask the NASA worm logo in S91-37110 and never show NASA insignia; no NASA endorsement implied; (2) do not caption the Pacioli letters as Leonardo's; (3) crop the printed headers and transcriptions off the facsimile pages. Rejected: 'Moon to Mars Infrastructure' (NASA HQ 2025): NASA meatball and worm logos plus a US flag, and a retro poster style; deleted. John J. Olson 1992 MSFC Mars base painting: artist's copyright status unclear. Smithsonian NASM A7-L suits: not in the Smithsonian Open Access CC0 metadata dump (NASM, 1,012 records), so not CC0. Hubble Mars portraits: ESA co-credit; Viking used instead. xEMU resource reel (NASA video): only 720p and shows named astronauts. No Italian-held works were used. Wikimedia Commons was not used, and the commons_direct.py helper named in the brief was not in the scratchpad. The metmuseum.org Open Access policy page returned HTTP 429, so the CC0 wording comes from the Met API docs and the isPublicDomain flag. Optional archival film: none taken; no faceless, high-resolution, public-domain clip was found in the time available.
